punchline: A robot learning and inspection workbench that connects demonstrations, simulation and guarded Intel deployment.
description:
## What we built
Prometheus connects the pieces needed to turn an SO-101 robot station into an inspection and sorting cell: demonstration collection, policy training, simulation, visual inspection and supervised deployment on an Intel laptop.

Our current imitation-learning task is to pick a block from clutter and place it on the blue plate. A separate Intel-side quality-sorting application implements perception, inspection and motion logic for good-to-blue and defective-or-uncertain-to-green routing.

## Robot learning pipeline
We prepared 64 real demonstrations with corrected task labels and reset-family splits: 41 training, 12 validation and 11 test episodes. Normalization uses training data only. Our 32-configuration experiment matrix compares ACT and SmolVLA, normal images and a causal target-X cue, four cumulative augmentation recipes, and real-only versus mixed real/simulation data. Real-data training has launched; synthetic-mixed runs remain gated on camera/contact validation.

The X cue starts from a selected target and disappears when tracking confidence fails. It is an experiment to reduce target ambiguity, not an assumed improvement. Augmentation changes training images online without treating duplicated frames as new demonstrations.

## Simulation and Intel integration
Our MuJoCo environment exposes object placement, camera views, contact and action traces. It supports expert collection, conversion to LeRobot data and policy evaluation. The presentation and video use clearly labeled simulation visuals, including a selected successful expert rollout.

We integrate with Physical AI Studio for collection and robot sessions, and include ACT/SmolVLA deployment utilities, OpenVINO inference checks and the Intel-side anomaly/inspection application. Shared output checks reject large or non-finite policy errors and constrain small overshoots without relaxing calibrated hardware limits.

## Verified progress and current limits
We have prepared and checked the data pipeline, executed simulation collection, run Intel inference checks and tested real policy-driven motion. Reliable physical grasp-and-place success and complete autonomous quality sorting have not yet been established. The full experiment comparison and any benefit from synthetic data remain to be measured. We do not claim measured power savings or NPU policy execution.

Source, calibration provenance, offline tests and evidence records make the implementation reviewable. The next milestone is comparable physical success trials across the same evaluation scenes, followed by selecting the augmentation and data variants that actually improve transfer.
